newsitem.title: UK: Russia catches up with Brady market rise.
newsitem.headline: Russia catches up with Brady market rise.

text.p: Emerging debt prices were firmer on Thursday and Russian paper was the biggest beneficiary of the market's renewed enthusiasm.
Fears over the health of President Boris Yeltsin have calmed, helped by the Kremlin's insistence that he is on the mend from pneumonia.
"Russia is basically catching up with the rest of the market this morning," one U.S. trader said, adding that much of the morning buying was from London, with sellers out of Moscow.
The debt market has been buoyant for most of this week, pushed up by fresh liquidity.
Dollar Vneshekonombank paper RUVNUSLNS=RR was up more than half a point. MinFins were also firmer.
Bulgaria continued to recover as investors grew more optimistic that the ruling Socialist Party will reach a compromise with the opposition which could put an end to the recent politicial chaos.

That in turn improves the chances of Sofia reaching a deal with the International Monetary Fund, so triggering an inflow of external finance and staving off the possibility of default later this year, one trader said.
Latin American debt held firm, with increased interest in Mexico after its announcement on Wednesday that it would pay off emergency loans from the U.S. and the IMF earlier than scheduled.
But Mexican Brady prices were barely changed in morning trading, after an initial rise in New York on Wednesday on the early repayment news.
